items.text: Iran launched drones at Kuwait and Bahrain on 18 Nov. The [[p:Islamic Republic of Iran Army|Artesh]] claims it hit Patriot systems at [[p:Ali Al Salem Air Base]], which hosts US forces; Kuwait says it intercepted the drones and Bahrain says it repelled several attacks. A US official says US aircraft struck an [[p:Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps|IRGC]] launch site on Qeshm on 17 Nov, and two officials say tit-for-tat strikes are now near-daily. No casualties reported.
items.notes: Iranian claims of hits are unverified; Kuwaiti and Bahraini statements say interceptions. US strike reported by officials, not officially announced.

items.text: The [[p:Israel Defense Forces|Israeli army]] launched what it called a concentrated operation in three areas of central Gaza near the 'yellow line', the first large operation there since the October 2025 ceasefire, closing parts of Salah al-Din Road. The US-backed [[p:Board of Peace]] told the UN Security Council the ceasefire could collapse and faulted both Israel and [[p:Hamas]].
items.thread: Gaza ceasefire and Board of Peace plan
items.notes: Operation details from IDF statement as relayed by Drop Site; Board of Peace warning cross-checked with Just Security digest. Reports of three Palestinians killed on 18 Nov not independently confirmed.

items.text: [[p:Donald Trump]] met [[p:Xi Jinping]] and [[p:Vladimir Putin]] separately, then held the first-ever US–China–Russia leaders' meeting in Shenzhen at [[e:APEC China 2026]]. Nuclear arms were the stated focus, but no formal agreement was reported and US officials had played down a deal. Trump and Xi agreed on the importance of restoring oil flows through Hormuz; the Kremlin said Putin left his Trump meeting in an 'excellent' mood.
items.notes: Outcomes still emerging at time of logging; the meeting ran on 19 Nov local time. Earlier Kremlin headlines conflicted on whether a full Trump–Putin bilateral would be held.

items.text: Democrats flipped both remaining Senate seats: [[p:Mary Peltola]] beat Sen. [[p:Dan Sullivan (American politician)|Dan Sullivan]] in Alaska, and AP had called Mississippi for [[p:Scott Colom]] over [[p:Cindy Hyde-Smith]] on 11 Nov, making him the state's first Black senator since Reconstruction. Democrats will hold 56 of 100 seats from January.
items.notes: Mississippi call predates the last segment day but was logged then as uncalled.

items.text: House Democrats nominated [[p:Hakeem Jeffries]] for Speaker on 18 Nov; he ran unopposed but drew objections from some newly elected left-wing members, many aligned with the [[p:Democratic Socialists of America]]. [[p:Katherine Clark]] and [[p:Pete Aguilar]] were unopposed for majority leader and whip.
items.notes: AP (Lisa Mascaro) preview confirms uncontested slate; vote tally not published.

items.text: New detail on the Carney–Xi tariff deal logged yesterday: in return for China's relief on about C$400m of pork and seafood, Canada extends by two years remission measures on some Chinese steel and aluminium due to expire at the end of 2026. Carney's office says market access is restored for over 90% of previously tariffed trade, about C$7.5bn.
items.notes: Figures from Carney's office. US adviser criticism appears only as a CP headline. Main deal already logged as E-261118-16; only new details recorded here.

items.text: Carney met [[p:Claudia Sheinbaum]] in Shenzhen to discuss stalled talks on the [[e:United States–Mexico–Canada Agreement|USMCA]], now under rolling annual review after Washington declined to renew it in July. USTR [[p:Jamieson Greer]] wants limited interim deals by year-end, but reports say Commerce Secretary [[p:Howard Lutnick]] has repeatedly blocked progress. Canada faces 50% US tariffs on some goods; Mexico has not retaliated.
items.notes: Lutnick blocking claim is attributed to unnamed reports. Carney is also expected to meet Trump at APEC (Just Security).

items.text: Health, education and university workers held a 12-hour national strike backed by more than 120 groups on 16 Nov, demanding living wages and a year-end bonus not tied to the minimum wage. Unions plan a 24-hour strike next week with a march on Miraflores if [[p:Delcy Rodríguez]]'s interim government does not respond. Separately, applications for 18 vacancies on the [[p:Supreme Tribunal of Justice]] closed on 18 Nov; the nominations committee's list is due on 11 Dec.
items.notes: Translated from Spanish. Second link covers the court timeline; strike reported by El Diario on 16 and 17 Nov.

items.text: Trinidad-based Cliper Group signed a 25-year deal with PDVSA to reactivate a Venezuelan oil field.

Back from Spain, Lula faces a decisive week: the Senate passed the base text of the fiscal adjustment bill (PLP 299/2026) 45–31, with four amendments that could strip savings left to vote before it goes to the Chamber, where its fate is uncertain. Lula may name some fourth-term ministers early, and faces pressure to fill a Supreme Court vacancy before a more right-leaning Senate arrives in 2027.
items.notes: Translated from Portuguese. Outcome of the 17 Nov amendment votes not yet confirmed.

items.text: US Vice President [[p:JD Vance]] cancelled a planned 20–21 Nov visit to Colombia, according to La FM and Blu Radio; no reason was given. October inflation rose to 6.30%, and talks on the 2027 minimum wage opened on 18 Nov. President [[p:Abelardo de la Espriella]] drew criticism for receiving six captured Frente 33 dissidents in Cúcuta while wearing camouflage.
items.notes: Translated. Vance cancellation relayed from La FM/Blu Radio; not confirmed by the White House.

items.text: [[p:Javier Milei]] confirmed at the Casa Rosada that he will seek re-election in 2027, promising further tax cuts and touting new trade talks with the EU, EFTA, Singapore and the US.

Haitian PM [[p:Alix Didier Fils-Aimé]] was due in El Salvador on 16–17 Nov to discuss the future of an estimated 2,000–2,500 Salvadoran troops, most operating outside the [[p:Gang Suppression Force]]; the deployment terms have not been published. Elections are now tentatively set for July 2027.
items.notes: Visit outcome not found; El Mundo (EFE) confirms the mid-November trip was planned.

items.text: The Pentagon failed its annual audit for the ninth straight year.
An internal IRS memo reported by the New York Times shows at least four criminal investigations into left-wing groups since last year.
British police said a US Army lieutenant colonel arrested in the UK on suspicion of spying for Russia is now in US military custody.
Fed Governor Lisa Cook's lawyer said she will not join a 14 Dec White House hearing on her firing unless Kevin Hassett is removed from the panel.
